commands.name: expirely
commands.summary: expirely tells you what expires next, before it breaks anything.
commands.usage:
expirely tells you what expires next, before it breaks anything.

Usage
  expirely <command> [flags]

Commands
  tls                     check the certificates TLS endpoints serve
  tls aws                 list the certificates in AWS Certificate Manager
  tls gcp                 list the certificates of a Google Cloud project
  help [COMMAND]          show the help of a command, as in expirely help tls

Examples
  expirely tls example.com api.example.com:8443
  expirely tls aws
  expirely tls gcp

Flags
      --version           print the version
      --json              print the version as JSON
  -h, --help              show this help

Each command lists its own flags with --help, such as expirely tls --help.

Docs: https://github.com/expirely-dev/expirely-cli

flags.description: print the version

flags.description: show this help

commands.name: expirely tls
commands.summary: expirely tls checks the certificates TLS endpoints serve and when they expire.
commands.usage:
expirely tls checks the certificates TLS endpoints serve and when they expire.

Usage
  expirely tls [flags] TARGET...
  expirely tls [flags] -f FILE
  expirely tls aws [flags]
  expirely tls gcp [flags]

Commands
  expirely tls aws        list the certificates in AWS Certificate Manager
  expirely tls gcp        list the certificates of a Google Cloud project
  expirely tls help       show this help; aws and gcp have their own --help

Examples
  expirely tls example.com api.example.com:8443
  expirely tls -f hosts.txt --warn-days 21
  cat hosts.txt | expirely tls -f - --json | jq .summary

Targets
  -f, --file PATH         read targets from PATH, one per line; - reads stdin
  A target is host, host:port, [ipv6]:port or https://host/path.
  The port defaults to 443.

Scan
      --warn-days N       flag certificates expiring within N days (default 30)
      --timeout DURATION  time each target has to answer (default 10s)
      --concurrency N     targets scanned at once (default 16)
      --ca-file PATH      also trust the CA certificates in this PEM file
      --revocation        also ask the CA of each trusted certificate whether
                          it was revoked, by fetching its CRL over HTTP

Output
      --json              print JSON; the default when stdout is not a terminal
      --details           add every certificate of each chain to the JSON
      --status LIST       show only these statuses, as a comma list: expired,
                          revoked, expiring, error, unknown, ok, or all (the
                          default; a declared agent gets all but ok)
      --fields LIST       keys to keep in each JSON result; target always stays
      --limit N           show at most N results, most urgent first
      --version           print the version
  -h, --help              show this help

Environment
  NO_COLOR=1              text without color
  EXPIRELY_AGENT=1        report as to an AI agent: JSON and no spinner;
                          0 turns the detection of agents off
  EXPIRELY_GITHUB=0       no job summary or annotations in GitHub Actions

Exit codes, over every result whatever --status, --fields and --limit show
  0 all ok, 1 expired, revoked or expiring, 2 usage error, 3 a target could
  not be read or an end date is unknown, 130 stopped by Ctrl-C

Docs: https://github.com/expirely-dev/expirely-cli

commands.name: expirely tls aws
commands.summary: expirely tls aws lists the certificates in AWS Certificate Manager and when they expire.
commands.usage:
expirely tls aws lists the certificates in AWS Certificate Manager and when
they expire.

Usage
  expirely tls aws [flags]

Examples
  expirely tls aws --profile production --region us-east-1
  expirely tls aws --profile production --region all
  AWS_PROFILE=production expirely tls aws --region us-east-1,eu-west-1

AWS
      --profile NAME      profile from the shared AWS config (default
                          AWS_PROFILE, or the default credential chain)
      --region REGION     a region, a comma list, or all for every enabled
                          region (default AWS_REGION or the profile's region)

Scan
      --warn-days N       flag certificates expiring within N days (default 30)
      --timeout DURATION  time allowed to read ACM (default 30s)

Output
      --json              print JSON; the default when stdout is not a terminal
      --status LIST       show only these statuses, as a comma list: expired,
                          revoked, expiring, error, unknown, ok, or all (the
                          default; a declared agent gets all but ok)
      --fields LIST       keys to keep in each JSON result; target always stays
      --limit N           show at most N results, most urgent first
  -h, --help              show this help

expirely tls aws only calls acm:ListCertificates and
acm:DescribeCertificate, plus ec2:DescribeRegions for --region all, and
changes nothing. A region it cannot read is listed in unreadable, and the run
exits 3 unless a certificate it read exits 1.

commands.name: expirely tls gcp
commands.summary: expirely tls gcp lists the certificates of a Google Cloud project and when they expire.
commands.usage:
expirely tls gcp lists the certificates of a Google Cloud project and when
they expire.

Usage
  expirely tls gcp [flags]

Examples
  expirely tls gcp --project acme-production
  GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=acme-production expirely tls gcp --warn-days 21

Google Cloud
      --project ID        project to read (default GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT or
                          CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT)

Scan
      --warn-days N       flag certificates expiring within N days (default 30)
      --timeout DURATION  time allowed to read the project (default 30s)

Output
      --json              print JSON; the default when stdout is not a terminal
      --status LIST       show only these statuses, as a comma list: expired,
                          revoked, expiring, error, unknown, ok, or all (the
                          default; a declared agent gets all but ok)
      --fields LIST       keys to keep in each JSON result; target always stays
      --limit N           show at most N results, most urgent first
  -h, --help              show this help

expirely tls gcp signs in with Application Default Credentials, lists the
Compute SSL certificates with their target proxies and the Certificate
Manager certificates in every location, and changes nothing. A region Google
cannot reach is listed in unreadable, and the run exits 3 unless a
certificate it read exits 1.

exit_codes.meaning: Every result is ok, or --help or --version ran.
At least one certificate is expired, revoked or expiring.
Usage error: unknown command, bad flag, invalid target, unreadable --file or no targets.
At least one target could not be read, an end date is unknown, a cloud command could not read every region, or writing the output failed.
Stopped by Ctrl-C before the end; no results were printed.

error_codes.cause: AWS refused the credentials, they expired, or they lack the ACM read permissions.
error_codes.remediation: The credentials were refused, expired or lack acm:ListCertificates and acm:DescribeCertificate in this account and region, or ec2:DescribeRegions for --region all.

error_codes.cause: expirely tls aws found no region in --region, AWS_REGION or the profile, or the profile does not exist in the shared AWS config.
error_codes.remediation: expirely tls aws reads the profile from --profile or AWS_PROFILE and the region from --region, AWS_REGION or that profile, as the AWS CLI does.

error_codes.cause: Another AWS failure, such as a timeout or a throttled request.
error_codes.remediation: ACM did not answer as expected; the message has its reason, and a later run or a longer --timeout often succeeds.

error_codes.cause: A --file could not be opened or read, or has a line over 64 KiB.
error_codes.remediation: A --file needs to exist, be readable and hold one target per line of at most 64 KiB; - reads stdin.

error_codes.cause: Google Cloud refused the credentials, or they lack the Compute or Certificate Manager list permissions.
error_codes.remediation: The credentials were refused or lack compute.sslCertificates.list, compute.targetHttpsProxies.list, compute.targetSslProxies.list, certificatemanager.locations.list or certificatemanager.certs.list in this project.

error_codes.cause: The project has the Compute Engine API or billing disabled, so it serves no Compute SSL certificates.
error_codes.remediation: Google Cloud reports the Compute Engine API or billing disabled in this project, so the project serves no Compute SSL certificates.

error_codes.cause: expirely tls gcp found no project, or no Application Default Credentials.
error_codes.remediation: expirely tls gcp reads the project from --project, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT or CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT and signs in with Application Default Credentials, as gcloud auth application-default login sets up.

error_codes.cause: Another Google Cloud failure, such as a timeout or a server error.
error_codes.remediation: Google Cloud did not answer as expected; the message has its reason, and a later run or a longer --timeout often succeeds.

error_codes.cause: The run was stopped, as Ctrl-C does, before it ended; it printed no results, since partial ones would read as complete.
error_codes.remediation: The run was stopped, as Ctrl-C does, before it ended; it printed no results, since partial ones would read as complete.

error_codes.cause: A --ca-file could not be read, holds no PEM certificate, or holds one that does not parse.
error_codes.remediation: A --ca-file is a readable PEM file with one or more CERTIFICATE blocks, such as an internal CA's root.

error_codes.cause: A flag is unknown or has a value it does not take.
error_codes.remediation: Each command lists every flag and the values it accepts in its --help.

error_codes.cause: A target is not a host, host:port or https:// URL.
error_codes.remediation: A target is host, host:port, [ipv6]:port or https://host/path; the port defaults to 443.

error_codes.cause: No target was given in the arguments or files.
error_codes.remediation: Targets come as arguments, such as expirely tls example.com, or one per line from --file.

error_codes.cause: Writing the result to stdout failed, for example a closed pipe.
error_codes.remediation: The reader of stdout closed before the output ended, as a pipe to head does; the scan itself finished.

error_codes.cause: expirely tls aws or expirely tls gcp got an argument that is not a flag, such as a target.
error_codes.remediation: expirely tls aws and expirely tls gcp read a whole account or project and take flags only; targets go to expirely tls.

error_codes.cause: The first argument is not a command, or expirely help got a command there is no help for.
error_codes.remediation: expirely --help lists the commands; checks run under expirely tls, such as expirely tls example.com, expirely tls aws and expirely tls gcp.

result_error_codes.remediation: A wrong host or port, a host that is down, or a firewall between this network and the host causes this; reason says which.
The port accepted a connection but did not complete TLS; it may serve plain HTTP, need another port or reject this client; reason says which.
